 Order

This is second application under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of the applicant in connection with Crime No.691/2022 registered at Police Station Chandan Nagar, Indore (M.P.)
under Sections 386, 342, 34, 420, 467, 468, 471 of IPC and Sec.25 of Arms Act.
2.
The first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn.
3. The present application is filed mainly on the ground that despite number of opportunities the complainant is not turning up in the witness box though he is being represented before this court.
On 16.1.2024 also complainant did not appear and the case has been adjourned to 12.2.2024.
4. As per the prosecution case, it is alleged that the accused persons abducted the complainant in a car and had taken him to a lonely place and he was forged to sign on blank papers.
Thereafter he was asked to call his wife also and two accused persons went to his wife and got signed documents.
It is alleged that the signatures were obtained on the point of gun and knife.

sentences.text: Counsel for applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated ind the present case.
A civil suit has already been filed by one Devendra Dubey in whose favour the alleged agreement to sell has been executed.
He has been falsely implicated as an accused in the present case.
The stamp papers were issued in the name of the complainant and his wife.
The prosecution has not recorded the statement of stamp vendor and notary.
The applicant is in jail since 1.9.2022 and the trial is likely to take time.
6. Counsel for State submits that the applicant has been identified by the complainant.
However, he fairly submits that the statement of stamp vendor and notary have not been recorded by the prosecution and they have not been cited as witness.
He is habitual offender as there are 5 criminal cases against him.
7. Counsel for Objector submits that the original of agreement was seized from the possession of the present applicant.

8. Upon perusal of the seizure memo, it is not clear that whether original or photocopy was seized from the possession of the applicant, the complainant has also filed an application before the trial court u/S.19(1) Cr.P.C for production of original copy of agreement.
9. After hearing learned counsel for parties it is found that the stamp papers are issued in the name of the complainant and his wife.
The alleged forged document is notarised, but the prosecution has not recorded the statement of stamp vendor and notary.
The complainant is not turning up in the witness box.
The applicant is in jail since 1.9.2022.
Trial is likely to take time.
10. Therefore, without expressing any view on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

11. It is directed that Applicant shall be released from custody upon furnishing a personal bond of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh Only) with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Ld. Court below on the condition that (1) the applicant shall not influence the complainant and his witness and shall not tamper with the evidence (2) the applicant shall mark his presence before the concerned police station on every 15th of the month during the trial.

12. It is further made clear that if it is found that the applicant is involved in any other case during the trial, this bail order shall stand cancelled automatically without reference to the Court and the Police will be at liberty to arrest the applicant.
13.
A typed copy of this order is being forwarded to the Office of the Advocate General, on their email address, for intimation to the Police Station concerned.
The office is requested to forward a copy of this order to the Ld. Court below.

(VIJAY KUMAR SHUKLA) JUDGE VM Arif Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109748499/
